questions.q: An agent summarises customer-submitted web pages and also holds a customer database tool. The team enables the web fetch tool so it can follow links in those pages. A security reviewer is concerned. Which concern and mitigation match the documentation?
options: Web fetch is safe in any environment because Claude cannot fetch a URL unless a person types it, so no extra controls on domains are needed
The only risk is cost, so the mitigation is to cap max_tokens and leave the domain list open for the model to choose where to fetch from
Untrusted input alongside sensitive data raises data exfiltration risk, so restrict fetching with allowed_domains and limit fetches per turn with max_uses
Move the customer database tool into the user turn as plain text, since tools in the user turn cannot be reached by instructions found on a page, however many pages the agent reads in a session
questions.explain: The docs warn that enabling web fetch where Claude processes untrusted input alongside sensitive data poses data exfiltration risks, and suggest limiting fetches with max_uses and restricting domains with allowed_domains.
questions.constraint: untrusted pages plus a sensitive tool plus web fetch
breaks: Claude cannot fetch URLs that appear only in its own output, but links in untrusted pages can still lead to risk
the documented concern is exfiltration, not only cost
tool access is not changed by placing text in a turn, and it removes the tool's function
questions.chapter: Security: injection, untrusted input, scoped identity and secrets

questions.q: A CI job runs Claude Code to review pull requests from external contributors. A PR description contains hidden text telling the reviewer to print environment variables and post them as a comment. The runner's environment holds a deployment token. Which combination best limits the damage?
options: Run the job with sandboxed shell commands, keep the deployment token out of that environment and give the job only the minimum repository permission it needs
Add a line to the review prompt saying that text inside pull request descriptions must never be obeyed, and keep the token in the environment

Trust the contributors who have previously merged code, and skip sandboxing for them because their descriptions are unlikely to contain hidden text, reviewing only first-time authors' pull requests with extra care
Switch to a larger model for reviews, since a more capable model is documented to recognise every injected instruction in a pull request body
questions.explain: Prompt injection works by inserting text that overrides the assistant's instructions, so the controls must hold even if the model is fooled: sandbox the shell with filesystem and network isolation, keep secrets out of reach and grant least privilege.
questions.constraint: hidden instructions in a PR body, secret in the environment
breaks: a prompt line is not an enforcement boundary and the token stays reachable
contributor reputation is not a technical control
no model is documented to be immune to injection
questions.chapter: Security: injection, untrusted input, scoped identity and secrets

questions.q: A public chatbot's only defence against users who try role-play tricks to extract policy-breaking answers is one paragraph in the system prompt. After a successful bypass, the team wants to improve resilience. Which design is the strongest?
options: Make the system prompt paragraph longer and more emphatic, since a single stronger instruction is the most reliable single defence against all the tricks that users might try
Block any user message that contains the words role-play, pretend or ignore, since those words always signal an attempt to bypass the policy
Layer defences: screen inputs and outputs with a separate check, keep sensitive actions behind code-level controls, and test with adversarial prompts
Remove the system prompt entirely, because with no policy text there is nothing for a user to override or extract from the conversation
questions.explain: No single instruction is a boundary. Defence in depth combines input and output screening, deterministic controls on sensitive actions, and adversarial testing so a bypass of one layer does not cause harm.
questions.constraint: single-paragraph system prompt bypassed by role-play
breaks: a longer prompt is still one layer that the next trick can bypass
keyword blocking is easy to bypass and rejects legitimate requests
removes the policy and every guardrail it provides
questions.chapter: Security: injection, untrusted input, scoped identity and secrets

questions.q: An engineer wants Claude Code's shell commands to be able to run package installs from the company's registry but not to reach arbitrary internet hosts, even if a prompt injection asks it to. Which control provides this regardless of the model's decisions?
options: Turn on sandboxing and set the network domains and filesystem paths that shell commands and their child processes may reach
Write in CLAUDE.md that only the company registry may be contacted, because instruction files are enforced by the operating system at runtime
Ask the model to confirm each hostname with the user in chat before running a command, and rely on users to notice a suspicious address
Disable Bash entirely and let Claude write scripts that the engineer runs by hand afterwards, since scripts cannot make network requests
questions.explain: The sandbox lets you set which files and network domains shell commands can reach, and the limits apply to the commands and the processes they start. That is deterministic enforcement outside the model.
questions.constraint: limit network reach independent of the model
breaks: CLAUDE.md is guidance to the model, not an operating-system control
relies on a person noticing and is not a boundary on the process
scripts can make network requests, and this removes the capability instead of limiting it
questions.chapter: Security: injection, untrusted input, scoped identity and secrets

questions.q: A reporting agent answers questions by running SQL. Its connection string is a database administrator account because that was quickest to set up. The team asks how to apply least privilege without changing the agent's prompt. What should they do?
options: Keep the administrator account but add a prompt rule forbidding DROP, DELETE and UPDATE statements, since the rule makes writes impossible
Log every statement the agent runs and review the log each week, because a log that is reviewed regularly prevents harmful statements
Run the agent against a copy of the production database refreshed monthly, and give the copy administrator rights so that nothing is restricted
Give the agent's connection a dedicated read-only role limited to the reporting tables, so unsafe statements fail at the database, regardless
questions.explain: Least privilege puts the limit where it cannot be talked around: a role that can only read the needed tables makes destructive statements fail, whatever the model is told. Logging detects, and prompt rules only ask.
questions.constraint: agent using a database administrator account
breaks: a prompt rule is not enforced by the database
logging detects after the fact and does not prevent
still grants full rights and gives stale data
questions.chapter: Security: injection, untrusted input, scoped identity and secrets

questions.q: A team stores a partner's signing secret and the internal admin URL in the system prompt of a customer-facing assistant, with a line saying never to reveal them. A tester extracts both with a few attempts. What is the right fix?
options: Add a stricter line to the system prompt and a second warning in the user turn, since two warnings are always enough to protect any secret
Keep secrets out of prompts entirely and hold them in server-side code the model cannot read, passing only what each call needs
Encode the secret in base64 inside the prompt, because the model cannot decode encoded strings and so cannot repeat them to a user
Tell the tester the secret was extracted by mistake and rotate it later, since secrets in a prompt expire after a few hours of exposure
questions.explain: Anything placed in a prompt can potentially be elicited, so secrets belong in server-side code and configuration that the model never sees. Once exposed, the secret should be rotated.
questions.constraint: secret and internal URL placed in a system prompt
breaks: more warnings are still not a boundary
models can decode base64
no such expiry exists, and the secret should be rotated now
questions.chapter: Security: injection, untrusted input, scoped identity and secrets

questions.q: A mobile app calls the Claude API directly from the phone, with the API key bundled in the app binary so that no backend is needed. A security audit flags it. What is the correct redesign?
options: Obfuscate the key inside the binary and rotate it every release, since an obfuscated string cannot be extracted by anyone who has the app
Route requests through a server-side proxy that holds the key, authenticates the user and applies per-user limits, so no key ships in-app
Store the key in the app's local storage after the first launch, because local storage on the phone is encrypted against other apps and users
Give every user their own key by email, so each person's usage is isolated and a leaked key harms only the one user who received it
questions.explain: A key embedded in client code is available to anyone who has the client. Keeping it on a server-side proxy lets the backend authenticate the caller, rate-limit, and revoke access without shipping secrets.
questions.constraint: API key bundled in a mobile app
breaks: obfuscated keys can still be extracted from an app binary
a key on the device remains within reach of anyone who controls it
distributing keys to users spreads the exposure and cannot be revoked in one place
questions.chapter: Security: injection, untrusted input, scoped identity and secrets

questions.q: A company runs development, staging and production services that each call Claude with the same organisation-wide key, so one team's load test used up shared limits and a leaked staging key exposed production. Which setup follows the guidance on workspaces and keys?
options: Keep one key but rename it per environment in the console, since the name of a key decides which workspace limits and permissions apply

Use an admin key in every environment, since an admin key is the standard credential for production calls and has the widest permissions across the whole organisation, which also keeps the number of keys to manage down to one
Put the three keys in a shared document so any engineer can pick the right one quickly when moving code from one environment to another
Create separate workspaces for each environment and issue API keys scoped to a single workspace, keeping admin keys for management and reporting only
questions.explain: Workspaces separate projects, environments and teams under central billing, and API keys can be scoped to a single workspace. Admin API keys authenticate calls that manage and report on the organisation, not ordinary application traffic.
questions.constraint: shared key across environments
breaks: a key's label does not scope its permissions or limits
an admin key is for managing and reporting on the organisation, not for application calls
spreads secrets widely and does not isolate the environments
questions.chapter: Security: injection, untrusted input, scoped identity and secrets

questions.q: A create_event tool takes a nested attendees array, an ISO 8601 start time with time zone, and a recurrence rule. Claude often passes the time as "tomorrow 3pm" and flattens the attendees into a string. The description already explains each field. What is the next most useful improvement?
options: Add input_examples with realistic complete inputs, because examples show Claude the exact format of nested and format-sensitive parameters
Shorten the description to one line so that Claude has less to misread, since long descriptions are documented to confuse tool selection
Rename the tool to a longer, more formal name, since the name alone decides how the model formats each of the parameters that it fills in
Move the format rules into the user's message each time, since the model reads user text more carefully than anything in the tool definition
questions.explain: Detailed descriptions come first, but for tools with complex inputs, nested objects or format-sensitive parameters the input_examples field shows Claude how to use the tool. The fix belongs in the tool definition, not in each user message.
questions.constraint: nested and format-sensitive tool parameters
breaks: descriptions are the most important factor, and shortening removes needed detail
the name does not control how parameters are formatted
puts tool-specific rules into every request instead of the tool definition
questions.chapter: Tool schemas, the tool-use loop and parallel calls

questions.q: A developer adds the web search server tool. After the first response, the code looks for a tool_use block for it, runs its own search and sends a tool_result back, and the API reports a conflict. What is the misunderstanding?
options: Server tools must be executed by the application exactly like client tools, so the defect is that the tool_result was sent in the wrong block order
Server tools run only when tool_choice is set to any, so the defect is a missing tool_choice field in the original request from the application
Server tools run on the platform and return their results inside the response, so the application does not execute them or send is_error results
Server tools return nothing to the application, so the answer must be assembled from a second request that asks the model to recall the search
questions.explain: A server tool is executed by Anthropic's platform, and its results (or errors) come back in the response. The application only executes client tools and only sends is_error tool results for those.
questions.constraint: application runs its own search for a server tool
breaks: the application does not execute server tools at all
tool_choice does not decide whether a server tool executes on the platform
the results are returned inside the response
questions.chapter: Tool schemas, the tool-use loop and parallel calls

questions.q: A model returns two tool calls in one turn: create_ticket and add_comment_to_ticket, where the second needs the ticket id produced by the first. The harness runs them concurrently, and the comment call fails. What is the correct handling?
options: Run them concurrently anyway and retry the second until the first finishes, since the API requires parallel execution for parallel calls
Drop the second tool call without telling the model, since a tool_use block without a matching result is simply ignored by the API

Disable tools for the rest of the conversation after any failure, because a failed call cannot be recovered within the same assistant turn, so the harness should stop offering tools after the first failure it sees
Run the dependent calls in order, and for any call you skip because an earlier one failed, still return a tool_result with is_error and a brief explanation
questions.explain: The API doesn't prescribe an order; tools with side effects or ordering requirements might better run sequentially. A call you choose not to run still needs a tool_result with is_error true and a short explanation, so the model sees what happened.
questions.constraint: second call depends on the first call's output
breaks: the API does not prescribe an execution order or require concurrency
every tool_use needs a tool_result, including skipped calls
a failure can be reported and recovered from
questions.chapter: Tool schemas, the tool-use loop and parallel calls

questions.q: A refund tool must not run until a manager confirms in the team's own approval screen. The team can implement the tool either as a client tool in their application or rely on a platform-executed tool. Which choice supports the approval pattern?
options: Use a server tool, because the platform executes it immediately and can be configured to wait for a manager's click inside the Anthropic console
Implement it as a client tool, so the application receives the call, shows the approval screen and only then executes it and returns the result
Implement it as a client tool but run it as soon as the call arrives, and ask the manager to confirm afterwards through the audit report
Describe the approval requirement in the tool description and execute the call immediately, since the model will obey the description each time
questions.explain: Client tools are executed by the application, so it controls when they run and can place human approval between the call and execution. Server tools run on the platform, and a description cannot enforce a pause.
questions.constraint: human approval before an irreversible tool runs
breaks: the platform runs server tools itself; the application cannot insert its own approval step
confirmation after execution cannot prevent an irreversible refund
a description is guidance, not an enforcement point
questions.chapter: Production agents: workflow vs agent, wiring and human checkpoints

questions.q: A company's inventory service must be reachable by Claude applications on many different machines and maintained independently by the platform team. Which MCP deployment fits?
options: A stdio server installed on each machine, since stdio servers are the recommended way to share one service with many remote clients
A server that is copied into each application's repository, so every team keeps its own version and updates it whenever it suits them
A remote MCP server over HTTP, which is the recommended option for connecting to remote servers from many clients, owned by one team
A prompt template in each application that describes the inventory API in text, so the model writes the calls itself without any server
questions.explain: HTTP servers are the recommended option for remote MCP servers, which suits one independently maintained service used by many clients. stdio servers run locally with their client.
questions.constraint: one service, many client machines
breaks: stdio servers run as local processes per client
defeats independent maintenance by one team
no live capability is provided and nothing is maintained centrally
questions.chapter: The StreamableHTTP transport

questions.q: An application built on the Agent SDK needs Claude to call three small Python functions that already live in the same codebase, with no need for any other application to use them. What is the simplest suitable integration?
options: Define them as custom tools in the SDK's in-process MCP server, so they run inside the application without a separate server process
Build a standalone remote MCP server with its own deployment and authentication, since any function Claude calls must live in a separate service
Describe the functions in the system prompt and ask Claude to emulate them, because the model can reproduce the code's behaviour accurately
Rewrite them as Skills with scripts and drop the application's own code, since a Skill is the only way to expose functions to an SDK agent
questions.explain: MCP servers can execute directly within the SDK application, and the SDK's in-process MCP server is the documented way to give Claude your own functions without running a separate process.
questions.constraint: three functions, one application
breaks: unnecessary infrastructure for functions used by one application
emulation does not run the real code
skills are not the only mechanism, and rewriting is far more work than needed
questions.chapter: MCP servers: tools, resources, prompts, transport and scope

questions.q: Analysts want to attach a database schema document to a Claude Code prompt in the same way they @-mention a file, and the schema is maintained by the data team in an MCP server. Which MCP capability should the server use?
options: Expose it as a tool with side effects, since only tools can be referenced in a prompt and resources are limited to server configuration data
Expose it as a prompt template, since templates are the only MCP feature that can hold a document as long as a database schema
Expose the schema as an MCP resource, which Claude Code lets users reference with @ mentions like a file, rather than as a tool
Bundle the schema into the server's startup logs, since log output is shown to the analysts' prompts automatically at the start of a session
questions.explain: MCP servers can expose resources that users reference with @ mentions, similar to files. Tools are for actions, and prompts are reusable templates, so a referenceable document is a resource.
questions.constraint: referenceable document from an MCP server
breaks: resources are the capability meant for referenceable data
prompts are reusable instruction templates, not referenceable data
logs are not surfaced in prompts
questions.chapter: Defining resources

questions.q: A remote MCP server adds a new tool while a Claude Code session is open and sends a list_changed notification. A developer asks whether they must restart the session to see the tool. What is correct?
options: No restart is needed: the server can change its tools, prompts or resources while connected and notify the client, which refreshes its list
A restart is required, because Claude Code reads the server's tool list once at start and ignores every later change in the server
The new tool appears only after the developer removes and re-adds the server, since a notification cannot change a registered server's tool list
The notification works only for stdio servers, so a remote HTTP server must always be restarted by its owner after any change to its tools
questions.explain: An MCP server can change the tools, prompts or resources it offers while connected and send a list_changed notification; the client refreshes without a restart.
questions.constraint: tool added to a connected server
breaks: servers can announce changes while connected
the notification exists so the client can refresh without re-adding
the notification is not limited to stdio servers
questions.chapter: MCP servers: tools, resources, prompts, transport and scope

questions.q: A team wants Claude to follow the company's quarterly-report format: section order, wording rules and a template file. There is no external system to query. The guidance should cost almost nothing in context until it is needed. Which mechanism fits?
options: An MCP server exposing the template as a tool, because a tool is the only mechanism able to hold a file that Claude reads during the task
A longer system prompt on every request, since always-loaded text is the lightest way to carry a large template for a rare task
A fine-tuned model that has memorised the format, since fine-tuning is the supported way to teach a company's document templates
A Skill, which packages instructions and resources and keeps only its name and description in context until it is triggered, at low cost
questions.explain: Skills package procedural guidance and resources for Claude to use when relevant; until one is triggered only its name and description occupy context. With no external system to reach, an MCP server is unnecessary.
questions.constraint: procedure and template, no external system
breaks: no external capability is needed, and a server adds operation work
always-loaded text costs context on every request
disproportionate, and the template cannot be updated as a file
questions.chapter: What are skills?

questions.q: A team needs Claude to look up live prices from an internal service owned by another team, usable by several of the company's Claude applications and agents, with changes shipped by the owning team. Which mechanism fits best?
options: A Skill in each application that embeds the pricing rules as text, because Skills keep live data in sync with the internal service
An MCP server maintained by the owning team, which every application connects to, since the capability lives outside any one app
A custom tool coded separately in every application, so each team controls its own integration and no one depends on another team
A longer system prompt listing last quarter's prices, since prices that change slowly never need to be fetched during a conversation
questions.explain: The deciding factors are where the capability lives, who maintains it and how Claude invokes it: a live internal service owned by another team and shared across applications is what an MCP server is for. Skills and prompts hold instructions, not live access.
questions.constraint: shared live capability owned by another team
breaks: text snapshots go stale and cannot call the service
duplicates the integration and diverges when the owner changes the service
stale text is not a live lookup
questions.chapter: Introducing MCP
